DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing Pancoast Syndrome.

The combination of a right upper lobe mass, focal weakness/sensory loss in the right arm, and significant weight loss in a smoker strongly suggests a lung malignancy invading the sympathetic chain and brachial plexus. The atrophy and pain pattern confirm the diagnosis.
